lesson_title: VAT Calculations: the Fifteen Percent Hiding in Every Price
hook_text: Shoes cost R299 with VAT inside. Take 15% off to find the real price? Congratulations, you just failed the question.
clip_script: Every price in the shop hides a tax. The shoes say R299 — but that's the price WITH the government's fifteen percent already baked in. Now the exam asks: what did they cost before VAT? Almost everyone does the natural thing — take fifteen percent off. 15% of 299 is 44,85, subtract, get R254,15. Wrong. Here's why: the fifteen percent slice was cut from the SMALLER number, the before-tax price — not from 299. Slice the big number and you cut too deep. The real move: R299 is 115% of the original, so DIVIDE by 1,15. That's R260 exactly. The VAT hiding inside? R39. And prove it — 260 times 1,15 runs straight back to 299. If your answer can't run forwards, it's wrong. One more secret from your till slip: brown bread, maize meal, milk, eggs — zero percent VAT, on purpose. White bread? Taxed. Frozen chips? Taxed. So sort the slip before you calculate. VAT on: times 1,15. VAT out: divide by 1,15. Never subtract fifteen percent. Ever.
visual_style: A till slip unrolling down the screen, standard-rated lines lighting up with red stars while zero-rated basics glow green; a loaf of bread gaining and losing a 15% slice; the wrong answer R254,15 stamped out and R260,00 stamped in.
mood: Streetwise and protective, the voice of someone who checks the slip before leaving the till.
pacing: Fast into the trap, a dead stop on the wrong answer, deliberate and clear through the divide-by-1,15 fix and the zero-rated reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make the 15% work for your marks, not against them.
